summary: Two columns of sections, side by side when the window is wide and one under the other when it is not. Each is as tall as its content, so it belongs on a scrolling screen; each part is written once, not once per layout. For two parts that fill a fixed window, use AdaptiveSplit.

sideAt.doc: Window width in dp from which they sit side by side

inset.doc: The horizontal padding around the call, both sides together: the columns share the window minus this

maxWidth.doc: The widest the two may get together; beyond it they stay centred

gap.doc: Space between the columns, across or down

ratio.doc: The first column's share of the width when side by side

first.doc: The first column, left or on top: a list of sections, stacked with the gap

second.doc: The second column, right or below

pitfalls: inset must match the padding around the call: flow wraps as soon as the two widths exceed the real space, and the columns stack on a wide screen
Decided by the window, not by content: a tall first column stays tall, with empty space under the shorter one
The slots cannot read s: to change content by layout, compute the same flag in the document
